$comment: Analytics taxonomy — error family. Merged with its siblings by server/analytics.taxonomy(); see _envelope.json.

desktop_error.$comment: Posted DIRECTLY to PostHog by desktop/main.js (the backend may never have started), so it does NOT pass through server/analytics.validate_event — main.js runs the same gate itself against this merged taxonomy. It used to send `message` (500 chars) and `stack` (8000 chars), which were undeclared and therefore unvalidated: a live free-text path to the wire. They are replaced by the classified triple below, the same pattern launch_failure already ships. Raw text stays in the local log and the fatal dialog.
desktop_error.question: Did the shell crash before the backend could report anything?

error_reported.$comment: The bounded, taxonomy-gated twin of the SDK's own `$exception`, which is diagnostic and ungated. `fatal` MUST be honored by wall #5's crash numerator — counting handled errors as crashes was the original defect. `fingerprint` groups on the exception CLASS plus the top frame's BASENAME, never the message: a message embeds ids and paths, so hashing it would give every occurrence its own group.
error_reported.question: One crash inbox — what is breaking, where, and is it fatal?

http_error.$comment: The CLIENT-side choke point. Every FastAPI HTTPException bypasses the backend's global exception handler, so this whole 4xx surface is invisible server-side. A per-session ROLLUP: uploading one event per 4xx would put a broken poll loop straight through the budget. The route TEMPLATE, never the concrete path — /api/projects/q4-launch-teaser/assets is the project slug.
http_error.question: The whole 4xx surface. Every 422 and 404 is a UX bug we cannot currently see.

network_operation_failed.$comment: NOT inside api.js's json(): json() runs only when the fetch RESOLVES, so offline / dns / tls / reset reject before a response exists and 5 of the 7 declared classes were unobservable there.
network_operation_failed.question: Where does connectivity break a local-first app?

data_quality_violation.$comment: Reported on the NEXT successful capture, never from inside validate_event — that would re-enter the validator on the event already being rejected. Bounded to one pending violation: the question is 'is the taxonomy drifting', and the first one answers it.
data_quality_violation.question: Is the taxonomy drifting away from the code?

open_vocabularies.exception_class: A JS/Python exception CLASS name (TypeError, ENOENT, RenderError). Produced by the runtime or by our own raise sites; never a message body. Bounded-token only, so a class name carrying prose fails the shape check and is dropped.
open_vocabularies.top_frame: basename:line of the topmost stack frame, e.g. `main.js:842`. The directory is stripped at the emit site because a full frame is /Users/<username>/..., i.e. the OS username. Our own source filenames; no user-input path.
open_vocabularies.fingerprint: ExceptionClass@basename:line, built at the emit site from the exception type and the top frame's BASENAME. No message body, no directory — the directory is /Users/<username>/.
open_vocabularies.event_name: An event name from this very taxonomy, or the undeclared name that was rejected. Bounded-token shape only, so a name carrying prose is dropped.
